title: Smart Traffic Management System
summary: A multi-modal system that fuses two YOLO models with acoustic siren detection, so emergency vehicles get prioritised before they are even visually confirmed.
problem: Urban traffic systems react too slowly to real-world conditions — congestion builds, emergency vehicles get delayed, and traffic lights don't adapt to what's actually happening on the road.
The goal was to build a system that sees and reacts to real conditions in real time.

approach.heading: Three specialised models
body: Designed a computer vision-driven traffic management system combining three specialized models: a primary YOLO model for vehicle detection and classification (cars, trucks, motorcycles, buses, ambulances), a secondary YOLO model dedicated to traffic light state recognition, and a YAMNet-based audio classification model to detect emergency vehicle sirens acoustically.

approach.heading: Hearing before seeing
body: The acoustic model catches emergency vehicles even before they're visually confirmed. Combining visual and audio signals let the system prioritize emergency response scenarios faster than a vision-only approach could.

contribution: Designed and built the system end-to-end as a graduation project — from selecting and training the YOLO models for vehicle and signal detection, to integrating the YAMNet audio pipeline, to architecting how the multiple model outputs combine into a single real-time decision system.
outcome: Built a functioning multi-modal AI system (vision + audio) for real-time traffic response — including emergency vehicle prioritization, a scenario with direct public safety impact.
learnings: This project was where I first worked with combining multiple model types into one coordinated pipeline, a pattern that shows up again in my later multi-agent work.
